## Pull request overview

Fixes blank rendering of the “Q1 Sales Performance” report in the console by extending the `@objectstack/spec` → `@object-ui/types` boundary mapping so `ReportViewer` receives the shape it expects.

**Changes:**
- Map spec report `label → title` and `columns[].field/aggregate → fields[].name/aggregation + showInSummary` in `ReportView`.
- Auto-generate default `sections` (summary + table) when missing.
- Strengthen `ReportView` integration test to assert table headers and data rows render.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ReportView.tsx | Adds spec→ReportSchema mapping and generates default sections for `ReportViewer`. |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ReportView.test.tsx | Adds assertions to ensure headers and rows actually render for the Q1 report. |

The `columns → fields` mapping only runs when `mapped.fields` is falsy. If metadata ever provides `fields: []` (empty array) alongside spec `columns`, this block will be skipped and the report can still render blank. Consider treating an empty `fields` array as “missing” (e.g., map when `!mapped.fields?.length`) and/or merging `columns` into existing fields.

`ReportViewer` renders sections via `report.sections?.map(...)` and only falls back to the default table when `report.sections` is `undefined`. With the current condition `if (!mapped.sections && mapped.fields)`, an empty array (`sections: []`) will prevent auto-generation and also suppress the fallback path, resulting in no content. Consider generating default sections when `sections` is missing *or empty* (e.g., `!mapped.sections?.length`).
